title: Oh and this goes for the Entr’Acte too! #Broadway #GypsyMusical #Audr...
transcript: This is a plea to anyone working on the current Broadway production of Gypsy. If you are not working on that production, you can just keep scrolling. But if that is you. Hi, I'm Ben. I've seen your show twice now. I absolutely love it. But there is one thing I think you really need to change, and that is the overture. In my opinion, Gypsy has one of the best overtures in all of musical theatre. And both times I've seen the show now, the overture has played while the house lights are still up and ushers are still seating patrons, which, of course, meant that the people around me were still having full conversations, because we have the short hand in theater that when the lights go down, that is when you stop talking. And so because the house lights are up, they're still having conversations. I think several people didn't even realize the overture had started, and when they did, it was like, mid overture. And I get that in today's day and age, it's sometimes hard to stop people from talking through overtures. They've kind of fallen out of fashion. But I think that by leaving the house lights up, you're just encouraging that behavior even more. And it's also creating a confusing experience for the audience, where it's like, has the show started? Has it not started? And I really do think that your show would be better served if you brought the house lights. Down. And then started the overture. So people know. Okay, the show is starting now. Let's prepare to go on this journey. It is a very small change that I think will go a long way.
reasoning: The creator explicitly states he's seen the show twice and absolutely loves it, but the entire video focuses on a production criticism about the overture staging. The love is clear but brief, while the critique dominates.
keyQuote: I've seen your show twice now. I absolutely love it.
